segments.text:
V. 33.
But a certain Samaritan came where he was—It was admirably well judged, to repreſent the Diſtreſs on the Side of the Jew, and the Mercy on that of the Samaritan. For the Caſe being thus propoſed, Self-intereſt would make the very Scribe ſenſible, how amiable ſuch a Conduct was, and would lay him open to our LORD's Inference. Had it been put the other Way, Prejudice might more eaſily have interpoſed, before the Heart could have been affected.
